testPlan.title: TP: On-node xiNAS agent lifecycle — boot + poll + publish
testPlan.scope: Covers the steady-state lifecycle of the on-node agent (xiNAS-MCP/src/agent): config resolution (config.ts), the Flow C boot sweep (boot.ts), the batching/retry/reconcile Publisher (publisher.ts), the poll/backstop driver (poll.ts), and convergence wiring (convergence.ts: buildConvergence/runConvergence). Focus is observable lifecycle behavior: what the agent POSTs to /internal/v1/observed and /internal/v1/agent_started, when it reconciles vs. skips, and how it survives a transient api/probe outage without losing or wiping observed state. Explicitly EXCLUDED: individual collector/probe parsing correctness (covered by their own suites), the RPC/task-apply path, xiRAID gRPC transport, and the api-side ingestion of observations.

risks.description: A failed initialSweep that reconciles an empty snapshot would make the api reconcile-DELETE every existing observed row for that kind, silently wiping good data on a transient probe failure.
Retry-exhaustion (api down) that does NOT mark kinds pendingReconcile leaves observed state permanently stale until process restart — a silent freeze with no error surfaced to the user.
Boot mode not restored (ceiling flush during boot) sends a partial complete_snapshots:[] batch that the api reconcile-deletes, causing boot-time data loss for any kind exceeding 256 entries / 1 MB.
runConvergence throwing on a startup boot failure (api briefly down) would produce an unhandled rejection and prevent event streams + poll backstop from ever starting, so the node never recovers.
Retrying a 4xx (structurally-wrong payload) wastes backoff and can amplify a malformed batch against the api.
PollDriver.start not being idempotent would double-arm intervals, doubling observation traffic and probe load per collector.
Debounce reset-on-each-enqueue (instead of leading-arm) could starve the queue under a continuous event stream, so a quiet-then-busy node never flushes.
Config resolution silently accepting a missing controller-id / token file would start an agent that cannot authenticate, failing every POST with 401 with no clear root-cause.
A single throwing collector inside a poll tick or boot sweep aborting the whole loop would take down observation for all other kinds.

testPlan.environment: Node.js (agent runtime) + vitest (xiNAS-MCP). Unit/integration level: a fake api over a Unix-domain socket (http server on socketPath) records POST bodies, statuses, and headers; fake collectors/probes with scripted initialSweep() results and injectable throws. Publisher constructed with retryBaseMs=0 and debounceMs=0 to make retry/flush deterministic; debounce tests set an explicit small debounceMs with fake timers. PollDriver constructed with backstopMs override. Fixture probe mode exercised via XINAS_AGENT_PROBE_MODE=fixture:<dir>. No privileged host access required; no real xiRAID/NFS.
testPlan.entryCriteria: Agent package builds (tsc) and the existing agent test suite (vitest run) is green on the target branch; a fake api UDS harness and fake collector helpers are available in src/__tests__; fixture directory for probe-mode tests is present.
testPlan.exitCriteria: All P0 and P1 cases pass. No case demonstrates observed-data loss (reconcile-delete on failed sweep, boot ceiling partial) or a silent freeze (missing pendingReconcile on exhaustion). runConvergence resolves (never rejects) under injected boot/registry/poll failures. Any P2 miss is logged as a known limitation with a follow-up.

testCases.title: Boot sweep sends one reconcile batch per collector and posts agent_started exactly once
testCases.preconditions: Registry with N collectors, each initialSweep() returning a known set of deltas; fake api returns 200 for /internal/v1/observed and /internal/v1/agent_started.
testCases.inputData: 3 collectors: Disk (2 deltas), Users (2 User + 1 Group delta), Filesystem (0 deltas). controllerId='ctrl-1'.

steps.expected: For each collector, exactly one POST /internal/v1/observed arrives carrying its deltas and complete_snapshots set to the union of the collector.kind + delta kinds.

steps.action: Inspect the recorded POST bodies in registration order.
steps.expected: Disk batch complete_snapshots=['Disk']; Users batch complete_snapshots covers ['User','Group']; Filesystem batch has deltas:[] and complete_snapshots=['Filesystem'].
Exactly one POST /internal/v1/agent_started with body {controller_id:'ctrl-1'}; it is the last request and fires once.

testCases.expectedResult: Each kind is reconciled with a single complete snapshot and the api receives exactly one agent_started signal, clearing its heartbeat startup-grace timer.
testCases.observability: Fake api request log (path, body); assert count of agent_started == 1; boot.ts:59-69.

testCases.title: Failed initialSweep is skipped — no reconcile, existing observed rows are NOT wiped
testCases.preconditions: Registry with a collector whose initialSweep() rejects (probe throws), plus one healthy collector.
testCases.inputData: NfsCollector.initialSweep() throws Error('nfsd socket refused'); DiskCollector returns 1 delta.

steps.expected: A structured error line is written to stderr with subsystem:'boot', event:'initial_sweep_failed', kind:'NfsSession', error containing 'nfsd socket refused'.
NO batch is sent for the failed collector's kind(s) — no complete_snapshots:['NfsSession'] appears, so the api never reconcile-deletes existing NFS rows.

steps.action: Confirm the healthy collector still reconciled.
steps.expected: Disk batch with complete_snapshots=['Disk'] is present; agent_started still posts once.

testCases.expectedResult: A transient probe failure surfaces via log/health but does NOT emit an empty complete snapshot; good observed data for that kind is preserved for the poll backstop to re-reconcile later.
testCases.observability: stderr JSON line initial_sweep_failed; assert absence of complete_snapshots containing the failed kind; boot.ts:39-58.

testCases.title: Publisher retries 5xx with exponential backoff, then marks kinds pendingReconcile on exhaustion
testCases.preconditions: Publisher with maxRetries=5, retryBaseMs=0 (deterministic, no real waits). Fake api returns 503 for every attempt.
testCases.inputData: One enqueued delta of kind 'Disk'; flush().

steps.action: Enqueue a Disk delta and call flush().
steps.expected: Exactly 5 POST attempts to /internal/v1/observed are made (attempt 0..4).
Returns true — the kind was added to pendingReconcile after retry exhaustion.
The promise resolves; no unhandled rejection is produced on the exhaustion path.

testCases.expectedResult: 5xx exhaustion is non-fatal: the batch is dropped but the affected kind is queued for reconcile so the next poll tick re-sweeps and heals the gap.
testCases.observability: Attempt counter on the fake api; publisher.pendingReconcile membership; publisher.ts:166-205.

testCases.title: Successful (2xx) flush clears pendingReconcile for batch kinds and requested snapshot kinds
testCases.preconditions: Publisher with 'Disk' and 'NfsSession' already in pendingReconcile. Fake api returns 200.
testCases.inputData: Enqueue a Disk delta; call flushWithSnapshot(['NfsSession']).

steps.action: Pre-seed pendingReconcile with Disk and NfsSession, enqueue a Disk delta, call flushWithSnapshot(['NfsSession']).
steps.expected: One POST with deltas=[Disk], complete_snapshots=['NfsSession'] returns 200.
Both return false — Disk cleared because it was in the batch, NfsSession cleared because it was a requested complete_snapshot.

testCases.expectedResult: On success the publisher clears the reconcile debt for both the kinds actually sent as deltas and the kinds requested as complete snapshots.

testCases.title: loadAgentConfig resolves and trims controller_id/agent_token; inline config short-circuits
testCases.preconditions: A temp config.json referencing controller_id_path and agent_token_path files whose contents have trailing newlines/whitespace.
testCases.inputData: controller-id file contents='ctrl-42\n'; token file contents='  secret-token  \n'; config includes nfs_helper_socket='/run/x.sock'.

steps.action: Call loadAgentConfig({configPath}) pointing at the temp config.
steps.expected: Returns AgentConfig with controller_id==='ctrl-42' and agent_token==='secret-token' (both trimmed), api_socket/agent_socket/socket_group passed through, nfs_helper_socket==='/run/x.sock'.
Returns the inline object verbatim without touching the filesystem (no path reads).

steps.action: Call loadAgentConfig() on a config with no nfs_helper_socket key.
steps.expected: Result has no nfs_helper_socket property at all (omitted, not undefined), per exactOptionalPropertyTypes.

testCases.expectedResult: Config resolution reads referenced secret files, trims them, honors the inline override, and omits the optional helper socket when absent.

testCases.title: Poll backstop re-sweeps and consumes pendingReconcile after the api recovers
testCases.preconditions: A collector whose initialSweep() returns a stable set; Publisher whose api first errors (kind lands in pendingReconcile via an earlier flush) then recovers to 200. PollDriver with a short backstopMs and fake timers.

steps.action: Drive an initial flush that exhausts retries so needsReconcile('Network') is true; then flip the fake api to 200.
steps.expected: pendingReconcile contains 'Network'.

steps.action: Start PollDriver and advance fake timers by backstopMs.
steps.expected: #sweep runs collector.initialSweep(), enqueues its deltas, and POSTs flushWithSnapshot(['Network']) which returns 200.
Returns false — the successful reconcile flush cleared the kind; observed state is healed without a process restart.

testCases.expectedResult: The poll tick is the 'next tick' the retry path waited on: it re-sweeps the kind, reconciles it, and clears the reconcile debt.
testCases.observability: Fake api request log; publisher.pendingReconcile; poll.ts:65-77 + publisher.ts:171-180.

testCases.title: 4xx response is not retried and does not mark the kind for reconcile
testCases.preconditions: Publisher maxRetries=5, retryBaseMs=0. Fake api returns 400 on the first attempt.

steps.action: Enqueue a Disk delta and call flush(); api replies 400.
steps.expected: Exactly ONE POST attempt is made — no retry loop.
Returns false — a structurally-wrong payload is dropped, not queued for reconcile (retrying/reconciling would just resend the same bad batch).

testCases.expectedResult: 4xx short-circuits: single attempt, no backoff, no pendingReconcile entry.

testCases.title: Network error (api socket down) is treated as 5xx — retried, then pendingReconcile
testCases.preconditions: Publisher pointed at a socketPath with NO listener (ECONNREFUSED), or a server that destroys the connection. maxRetries=3, retryBaseMs=0.

steps.action: Enqueue and flush() against a dead api socket.
steps.expected: req.on('error') fires each attempt; the publisher performs maxRetries attempts (lastStatus reset to 0), never throwing out of flush().
Returns true — a connection error is handled identically to 5xx and lands the kind in pendingReconcile.

testCases.expectedResult: A transport-level failure is absorbed like a 5xx: bounded retries, no throw, reconcile debt recorded for recovery.

testCases.title: loadAgentConfig throws a clear error when config, controller-id, or token file is missing
testCases.preconditions: Temp paths crafted so each required file can be independently removed.
testCases.inputData: Case A: configPath does not exist. Case B: config exists but controller_id_path missing. Case C: config exists but agent_token_path missing.

steps.expected: Throws Error message 'xinas-agent config not found at /no/such.json'.
Throws 'controller-id file not found at <path>'.
Throws 'agent-token file not found at <path>'.

testCases.expectedResult: Each missing prerequisite fails fast with a path-specific message rather than starting an agent that cannot authenticate.

testCases.title: Boot mode suppresses ceiling/debounce auto-flush so an oversized kind is one reconcile batch
testCases.inputData: Enqueue 300 deltas of kind 'User' while in boot mode, then flushWithSnapshot(['User']).

steps.expected: No POST is made during the enqueues — the 256-entry ceiling does NOT trigger an early flush, and no debounce timer is armed.
A single POST carries all 300 deltas with complete_snapshots=['User'] — one reconcile batch, no partial complete_snapshots:[] flush precedes it.

testCases.expectedResult: Boot data is never lost to a partial ceiling flush: the whole kind is delivered as one atomic reconcile.
testCases.observability: POST count during enqueue phase == 0; final batch deltas.length == 300; publisher.ts:82-95.

testCases.title: Boot mode is restored (finally) even when a mid-boot flush throws
testCases.preconditions: Publisher stub whose flushWithSnapshot rejects on the first collector; setBootMode spy.
testCases.inputData: 2 collectors; publisher.flushWithSnapshot throws Error('boom') on the first call.

steps.action: Call runBootSequence and let the first flushWithSnapshot reject.
steps.expected: runBootSequence rejects/propagates, but publisher.setBootMode(false) was invoked in the finally block.
Sequence is setBootMode(true) then setBootMode(false); the publisher is left in steady-state mode so debounce/ceiling resume.

testCases.expectedResult: A boot flush failure cannot strand the publisher in boot mode (which would freeze steady-state auto-flush).

testCases.title: Empty collector still reconciles its primary kind to empty
testCases.preconditions: A collector whose initialSweep() returns []. Fake api 200.

steps.action: Run runBootSequence with the empty collector.
steps.expected: A POST is still sent with deltas:[] and complete_snapshots=['Filesystem'].
Because completeSnapshots.length>0, the empty-queue guard (queue.length===0 && completeSnapshots.length===0) does not skip the flush.

testCases.expectedResult: An empty sweep is a deliberate 'reconcile to zero rows', not a no-op — the api learns the kind has no entities.
testCases.observability: POST body deltas:[] with the kind in complete_snapshots; publisher.ts:150 + boot.ts:62-63.

testCases.title: Dual-kind collector marks ALL its kinds complete in one boot batch
testCases.preconditions: A collector.kind='User' whose sweep also emits 'Group' deltas.
testCases.inputData: UsersCollector.initialSweep() => [User a, User b, Group g1].

steps.expected: One POST with deltas=[User a, User b, Group g1] and complete_snapshots as the set {'User','Group'} (union of collector.kind and delta kinds).

steps.action: Assert both kinds present in complete_snapshots.
steps.expected: Neither 'User' nor 'Group' is left un-reconciled, so a stale Group from a prior run is reconcile-deleted correctly.

testCases.expectedResult: A collector that produces more than one kind reconciles every kind it owns, not just its declared primary.

testCases.title: PollDriver arms one interval per collector (pollIntervalMs vs 5-min backstop), start is idempotent, stop clears timers
testCases.preconditions: Registry with collector A (pollIntervalMs=30000) and collector B (no pollIntervalMs). Fake timers.

steps.expected: Two timers: A at 30000 ms, B at 300000 ms (DEFAULT_BACKSTOP_MS); each timer.unref() was called.
No additional timers armed — the #started guard makes the second call a no-op (no doubled traffic).
All intervals cleared, internal timer list emptied, #started reset so a later start() re-arms.

testCases.expectedResult: Each collector gets exactly one refresh timer at its own cadence or the shared backstop; start/stop are safe to call repeatedly.

testCases.title: A throwing collector in a poll tick is absorbed and does not break other collectors' timers
testCases.preconditions: Registry with collector X whose initialSweep() throws and collector Y that succeeds. Fake timers.
testCases.inputData: X.initialSweep() throws Error('probe gone'); Y returns 1 delta.

steps.action: Start PollDriver and fire X's tick.
steps.expected: The error is caught inside #sweep and logged as event:'poll_sweep_failed' with kind X and the error message; the interval callback does not throw.
Y sweeps, enqueues, and flushes normally — X's failure did not disarm or crash Y's timer.

testCases.expectedResult: Per-collector fault isolation: one bad probe degrades only its own kind, and its next tick retries.

testCases.title: runConvergence never rejects when the boot sweep fails at startup (api down)
testCases.preconditions: A Convergence whose runBootSequence rejects (api socket down at startup); registry.start and pollDriver.start are spies.
testCases.inputData: Publisher pointed at a dead api socket so the boot postOnce/flush path fails.

steps.action: await runConvergence(c) and assert it resolves.
steps.expected: The returned promise resolves (no unhandled rejection); a log line event:'boot_sequence_failed' is emitted.
registry.start(emit) and pollDriver.start() are both still invoked after the boot failure, so event streams and the poll backstop come up and later heal the observed state.

testCases.expectedResult: A transient startup failure is logged and absorbed; convergence always brings up the steady-state loop so the node self-heals once the api returns.
testCases.observability: Promise resolves; boot_sequence_failed log; registry.start/pollDriver.start spies; convergence.ts:420-446.

testCases.title: Steady-state debounce is leading-arm — a burst of enqueues produces a single flush
testCases.preconditions: Publisher with debounceMs=75, not in boot mode. Fake timers. Fake api 200.
testCases.inputData: Enqueue 10 Disk deltas in rapid succession, each below the 256/1MB ceiling.

steps.action: Enqueue 10 deltas within the debounce window without advancing timers.
steps.expected: No POST yet; exactly one debounce timer is armed on the FIRST enqueue and NOT reset by the subsequent nine (leading-arm).
Exactly one POST /internal/v1/observed carries all 10 deltas; the queue is drained and the timer is cleared.

steps.action: Enqueue once more and advance 75 ms.
steps.expected: A new single flush fires — the window re-arms for the next burst; a continuous stream cannot starve the flush.

testCases.expectedResult: Bursts coalesce into one flush per window and a quiet single event still flushes after the window, with no per-event chattiness or starvation.
testCases.observability: POST count vs. advanced time; setTimeout spy call count == 1 per window; publisher.ts:112-120.

testCases.title: Fixture probe mode spawns no subprocesses and populates disks/users/nfs-idmap from fixtures
testCases.preconditions: XINAS_AGENT_PROBE_MODE=fixture:<dir> with disk/users/nfs-idmap JSON fixtures present; a spy/guard that fails the test if any child_process spawn occurs.

steps.action: Set the env var and call buildConvergence(config); run the boot sweep against a fake api.
steps.expected: No subprocess is spawned (all probes are fixture-backed); the registry is fully constructed.

steps.action: Inspect observations for Disk, User/Group, NfsIdmap.
steps.expected: Those kinds are populated from the fixture files; other kinds sweep empty (fixture mode intentionally leaves them empty).

testCases.expectedResult: Fixture mode gives a hermetic, host-free agent for e2e/CI: real collector adapters, fixture data, zero privileged calls.
testCases.observability: spawn spy count == 0; observed rows for the three kinds; convergence.ts:121-131.

testCases.title: Observation POST body and headers carry the correct envelope and bearer auth
testCases.preconditions: Publisher with controllerId='ctrl-9', agentToken='tok-abc'. Fake api records headers and body.

steps.action: Trigger the flush and capture the recorded request.
steps.expected: Body JSON has keys observed_at (ISO 8601), controller_id==='ctrl-9', deltas (array), complete_snapshots===['Disk'].
Authorization==='Bearer tok-abc', Content-Type==='application/json', Content-Length matches the body byte length; request targets socketPath, path '/internal/v1/observed', method POST.

testCases.expectedResult: The wire contract to the api is exact: authenticated, correctly framed, and carries the controller id + reconcile set.
testCases.observability: Recorded headers/body on the fake api; publisher.ts:156-161, 208-232.
